title: Flash Flood Warning

details.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* Until 415 PM MDT.

heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.4 and 0.8 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1
hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow
moving through the Babylon Burn Scar. The debris flow can consist of
rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...

details.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and
ditches in the Babylon Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry arroyos is likely. The heavy rains
will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.

title: Heat Advisory
location: Guadalupe Mountains of Eddy County; Eddy County Plains; Loving; Ward; Guadalupe Mountains Above 7000 Feet; Guadalupe and Delaware Mountains; Eastern Culberson County; Reeves County Plains; Chinati Mountains; Davis Mountains

details.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures up to 107.

* WHERE...Guadalupe Mountains of west Texas and Southeast New Mexico,
Eddy County Plains, Loving, Ward, Eastern Culberson, Reeves County
Plains, Chinati Mountains, and Davis Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MDT /9 PM CDT/ Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses. Extreme heat
will significantly increase the potential for heat related
illnesses, particularly for those working or participating in
outdoor activities.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids even if you don't feel thirsty, but avoid
alcohol and caffeine. Stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on elderly and vulnerable relatives and
neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Look before you lock! Do not leave young children and pets in
unattended vehicles for even a moment. Car interiors will very
quickly reach lethal temperatures.

Rensselaer, moving east at 50 mph.

mobile homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

* Locations impacted include...
Plymouth, Monticello, Knox, Winamac, Monon, North Judson, Argos,
Brookston, Culver, Wanatah, Wolcott, Francesville, Royal Center,
Hamlet, Medaryville, La Crosse, Koontz Lake, Pulaski, Oak Grove,

from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado go at once into the

title: Flood Advisory
location: Beaufort, NC; Hyde, NC; Martin, NC; Tyrrell, NC; Washington, NC

details.description:

* WHERE...A portion of eastern North Carolina, including the
following counties, Beaufort, Hyde, Martin, Tyrrell and Washington.

* WHEN...Until 600 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 3 inches of rain have
fallen.

over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.

details.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

title: Special Weather Statement

details.description:

of Washington, moving south at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Up to 40 mph wind, pea sized hail and frequent cloud to
ground lightning.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect minor damage to tree limbs and blowing around of
light, unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Washington, Rayle, Ficklin, Newtown, Lundberg, Celeste, Lyneville,
Philomath, Sandy Cross, and Carters Grove.
details.instruction:
People outdoors should seek shelter immediately. If you can hear
thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

title: Flash Flood Warning
location: Lake, IN

details.description:
FFWLOT

The National Weather Service in Chicago has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Lake IN County in northwestern Indiana...

* Until 600 PM CDT.

* At 157 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Rapid-onset flooding of creeks, streams, drainage

other poor drainage areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hammond, Gary, Portage, Merrillville, East Chicago, Schererville,
Hobart, Crown Point, Highland, Munster, Cedar Lake, Lowell,

details.instruction:
A Flash Flood Warning means rapid-onset flooding is imminent or may
already be occurring. Persons along creeks, drainage ditches, and
other waterways should take immediate precautions to protect life
and property.

title: Beach Hazards Statement
location: Sheboygan; Ozaukee; Milwaukee; Racine; Kenosha

details.description:
* WHAT...Life threatening waves of 4 to 6 feet and dangerous
currents are expected.

* WHERE...Sheboygan, Ozaukee, Milwaukee, Racine and Kenosha
Counties.

* WHEN...From late Monday night through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming conditions are expected due to
high waves and onshore winds.
details.instruction:
Stay out of the water and away from dangerous areas like piers
and breakwalls.  Strong structural and longshore currents are
expected.  Rip currents are possible.

title: Extreme Heat Warning
location: Bolivar; Sunflower; Leflore

details.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with heat index values in excess
of 110 degrees.

* WHERE...Portions of north central and northwest Mississippi.

* WHEN...For the first Extreme Heat Warning, until 9 PM CDT this
evening. For the second Extreme Heat Warning, from 10 AM to 9 PM
CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat and high humidity events.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.
